text:
maria: Ran a multiplex regional fanout bench for the 13B open model (int8 q8x4) across A100/H100. Goal: compare prefill vs decode latency, tokens/sec, and $/1M tokens across regions. Posting short summary + raw numbers. Looking for kernel recs and sizing advice.

benchbot: Auto-summary (from run 2026-03-19 22:14 UTC):
```
Config: 13B q8x4, beamless decode, batch=1, concurrent clients=50, kv-cache enabled
Regions: us-east-1 (aws), eu-west-1, ap-northeast-1
GPUs: A100 (80GB), H100 (80GB), identical instance types per region
Workload: 50/50 mix single-turn prefill (long prompt ~1.2k tokens) + decode (avg 128 tokens)
Metrics collected: tokens/s (avg), p50/p95/p99 latency for prefill and decode, cost normalized ($/1M tokens)
```

Results (per-GPU normalized):

us-east-1:
- H100: decode tokens/sec = 9.1k, prefill p50=48ms, prefill p95=260ms, prefill p99=420ms, decode p50=12ms, decode p95=110ms, decode p99=320ms, $/1M tokens = $7.6
- A100: decode tokens/sec = 6.2k, prefill p50=78ms, prefill p95=420ms, prefill p99=760ms, decode p50=20ms, decode p95=190ms, decode p99=560ms, $/1M tokens = $5.0

eu-west-1 (latency penalty +10% & pricing +15%):
- H100: tokens/sec = 8.3k, $/1M = $8.7
- A100: tokens/sec = 5.6k, $/1M = $5.8

ap-northeast-1 (latency penalty +18% & pricing +22%):
- H100: tokens/sec = 7.5k, $/1M = $9.3
- A100: tokens/sec = 4.9k, $/1M = $6.2

Notes: cost here factors instance hourly + observed throughput; we normalized to 1M tokens given empirical tokens/sec under our steady-state mix. Prefill dominates compute when KV-hit < ~25% (we saw prefill CPU/GPU time ~2.8x single decode chunk).

kevin: Nice summary. A few quick Qs: 1) which attention/kernel impl was used? 2) did you force matmul fallback or use flash-attn/triton fused kernels?

maria: We used runtime default kernel selection: flash-attn-v2 where available, fallback to matmul for long-prefill segments. We also toggled a run forcing 'kernel=matmul' to measure worst-case.

sam: Did you capture KV-cache hit sensitivity? If we increase KV hit rate to 60-80%, how do numbers shift for cost/latency?

benchbot: KV sensitivity sweep (short):
- KV hit 10%: prefill tokens/sec drop ~12% vs baseline; prefill latency p99 ~ +10-20%
- KV hit 60%: system shows decode-dominated cost; tokens/sec effectively +18% on H100, +12% on A100; $/1M drops ~15% for H100, ~10% for A100
- Cold-start (KV hit ~0): H100 advantage increases for p99 (H100 p99 decode ~320ms vs A100 560ms) but cost gap widens moderately because H100 hourly price > A100

oliver: For capacity sizing: if target steady QPS is 120 active users (mix above) with average session sending 1 prefill + 3 decodes, and desired p95 decode < 250ms globally, my rough calc:
- US-heavy traffic: use 1 H100 per 100 concurrent decode streams (gives headroom), fallback A100 for background cheaper pool.
- Mixed region: A100 pool sized for throughput (1 A100 per ~60 concurrent decode streams), with autoscale-trigger to H100 when p95 crosses threshold.

kevin: Any kernel fallbacks observed that caused step-changes in latency? e.g., flash-attn->matmul when seq_len > X?

maria: Yes - long prompts (>1.5k tokens) cause flash-attn to fall back on our current runtime to matmul for the prefill chunk; that increases prefill time by ~2.5x on both HWs. Also we saw a kernel failure in ap-northeast slot during one run that forced a matmul fallback for decode chunks >512, spiking p99. Filed infra ticket #INF-5421.

sam: Any quality regressions with int8 q8x4 at this model size? We need to ensure weigh-in on evals before recommending quant for production.

maria: Quick A/B: BLEU-like proxy and a handful of golden prompts showed no meaningful degradation for the q8x4 profile in our sample set (n=200). But we flagged a small delta on long-token-gen coherence for some prompts — recommend gating with eval set before rollout.

oliver: Ops / cost playbook suggestion:
- Default: A100 pool for most workloads (cost-efficient) + small H100 pool for low-p99 critical endpoints.
- Autoscale policy: scale H100 when p95 decode > 200ms OR when error-rate > 0.5% for top-10 routes.
- Kernel policy: prefer flash-attn-v2; pin matmul-only for legacy fallback lanes.

kevin: For the runtime team: can we add a kernel-selection telemetry flag in traces so we can correlate p99 spikes with 'used_kernel=matmul' ?

maria: Yep, have an RFC ready and will open PR this week. Patch will add kernel metric tags + region-specific sampling.

benchbot: Full raw logs + CSV attached to the bench run (s3://redwood-bench/multiplex/1749999999/).

sam: TL;DR decision summary?

maria: TL;DR:
- H100 gives ~1.45-1.6x tokens/sec vs A100 for this 13B int8 profile and significantly better p99 tail for decode-heavy low-concurrency endpoints.
- A100 is materially cheaper $/1M tokens in steady throughput-heavy scenarios; use it as default for bulk inference.
- Prefill latency is sensitive to long prompts and kernel fallbacks — guard with prompt-length routing or pre-warm strategies.
- Recommend eval gating for q8x4 on long-coherence tests before wide rollout.

kevin: +1 to kernel telemetry. Also +1 to prompt-length routing rule.

maria: Thanks — I'll prepare a short notes doc with recommended autoscale thresholds and a small runbook for switching flows between A100/H100 pools.

oliver: Adding ops note: test the H100 fallback path under simulated infra failure every week (chaos test) to ensure graceful degradation.

maria: Cool. Closing this thread once I drop the doc (ETA tomorrow). :thumbsup:
